lines.text: //   Some important concepts to understand to use this library:

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         Characters are defined by unicode codepoints, e.g. 65 is

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         uppercase A, 231 is lowercase c with a cedilla, 0x7e30 is

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         A visual character shape (every codepoint is rendered as

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         A font-specific integer ID representing a glyph

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         Glyph shapes are defined relative to a baseline, which is the

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         bottom of uppercase characters. Characters extend both above

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         As you draw text to the screen, you keep track of a "current point"

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         which is the origin of each character. The current point's vertical

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         position is the baseline. Even "baked fonts" use this model.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         The vertical qualities of the font, used to vertically position

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         and space the characters. See docs for stbtt_GetFontVMetrics.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      Font Size in Pixels or Points

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         The preferred interface for specifying font sizes in stb_truetype

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         is to specify how tall the font's vertical extent should be in pixels.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         If that sounds good enough, skip the next paragraph.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         Most font APIs instead use "points", which are a common typographic

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         measurement for describing font size, defined as 72 points per inch.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         stb_truetype provides a point API for compatibility. However, true

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         "per inch" conventions don't make much sense on computer displays

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         since different monitors have different number of pixels per

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         inch. For example, Windows traditionally uses a convention that

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         there are 96 pixels per inch, thus making 'inch' measurements have

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         nothing to do with inches, and thus effectively defining a point to

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         be 1.333 pixels. Additionally, the TrueType font data provides

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         an explicit scale factor to scale a given font's glyphs to points,

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         but the author has observed that this scale factor is often wrong

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         for non-commercial fonts, thus making fonts scaled in points

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //         according to the TrueType spec incoherently sized in practice.

lines.text: // These functions compute a discretized SDF field for a single character, suitable for storing

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // in a single-channel texture, sampling with bilinear filtering, and testing against

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // larger than some threshold to produce scalable fonts.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //        scale             --  controls the size of the resulting SDF bitmap, same as it would be creating a regular bitmap

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //        glyph/codepoint   --  the character to generate the SDF for

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //        padding           --  extra "pixels" around the character which are filled with the distance to the character (not 0),

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //                                 which allows effects like bit outlines

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //        onedge_value      --  value 0-255 to test the SDF against to reconstruct the character (i.e. the isocontour of the character)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //        pixel_dist_scale  --  what value the SDF should increase by when moving one SDF "pixel" away from the edge (on the 0..255 scale)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //                                 if positive, > onedge_value is inside; if negative, < onedge_value is inside

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //        width,height      --  output height & width of the SDF bitmap (including padding)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //        xoff,yoff         --  output origin of the character

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //        return value      --  a 2D array of bytes 0..255, width*height in size

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // pixel_dist_scale & onedge_value are a scale & bias that allows you to make

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // optimal use of the limited 0..255 for your application, trading off precision

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // and special effects. SDF values outside the range 0..255 are clamped to 0..255.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      This will create an SDF bitmap in which the character is about 22 pixels

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      high but the whole bitmap is about 22+5+5=32 pixels high. To produce a filled

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      shape, sample the SDF at each pixel and fill the pixel if the SDF value

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      is greater than or equal to 180/255. (You'll actually want to antialias,

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      which is beyond the scope of this example.) Additionally, you can compute

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      offset outlines (e.g. to stroke the character border inside & outside,

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      or only outside). For example, to fill outside the character up to 3 SDF

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      pixels, you would compare against (180-36.0*3)/255 = 72/255. The above

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      choice of variables maps a range from 5 pixels outside the shape to

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      2 pixels inside the shape to 0..255; this is intended primarily for apply

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      outside effects only (the interior range is needed to allow proper

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: //      antialiasing of the font at *smaller* sizes)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // The function computes the SDF analytically at each SDF pixel, not by e.g.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // building a higher-res bitmap and approximating it. In theory the quality

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // should be as high as possible for an SDF of this size & representation, but

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // unclear if this is true in practice (perhaps building a higher-res bitmap

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // and computing from that can allow drop-out prevention).

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // The algorithm has not been optimized at all, so expect it to be slow

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // if computing lots of characters or very large sizes.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: // You should really just solve this offline, keep your own tables
